source.title: Patronus: Safeguarding Text-to-Image Models Against Adversarial Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Xin-Feng Li; Sheng-Yuan Pang; Jialin Wu; Jiangyi Deng; H. Zhong; Yan-Jiao Chen; Jie Zhang; Wen-Yuan Xu

page_placements.theme: Text-to-image concept safeguards are conditionally reversible

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation; full paper text, including appendix and references, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether malicious fine-tuning restores unsafe generation in text-to-image models, a different modality from the chat models specified in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports fine-tuning outcomes for text-to-image models, not chat models. Its results therefore do not directly test the claim versions as worded. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-prefill effects, localized safety weights, or the effects of benign fine-tuning on harmful compliance.
record.test_reason: The study covers text-to-image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion U-Net and decoder), not safety-trained chat or language models. No row measures any version's behaviour in the kind of system the versions name. Its fine-tuning results are part of a defense (mitigation) evaluation: baselines ESD and SafeGen serve as comparators to PATRONUS. It is therefore a related analogue, not a test of V1 or V7, and the reader's 'tests/T3' conflicts with its own all-'none' row links.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors report ESD and SafeGen compromised after about 2 and 10 fine-tuning iterations respectively. They also claim PATRONUS raises the attack budget by 10x data and 25x computation.
record.recipe_differences: A text-to-image defense combining a conditional decoder with non-fine-tunability training; the study does not reproduce the chat-model methods or token-position measurements in the claim's original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported robustness tests vary fine-tuning data size, iteration budget, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, LoRA rank, and unsafe category.

fits_no_version.finding: T2I alignment defenses (ESD, SafeGen) regain unsafe generation after 1–10 fine-tuning iterations on 200 NSFW image-caption pairs. The CLIP score rises to 32.5 and 34.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In text-to-image diffusion models, concept-erasure alignment is removed by small-scale harmful fine-tuning (analogue of V1).

fits_no_version.finding: Meta-learned non-fine-tunable training (PATRONUS) keeps unsafe CLIP scores near 17.5 under the same attack. The authors say it resists fewer than 2000 samples and 500 iterations, then occasionally fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In T2I models, adversarial (min-max) anti-fine-tuning training raises the attack budget about 10x in data and 25x in compute but does not prevent eventual compromise (analogue of V7).

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
record.problems: The experiments concern text-to-image models rather than chat models. The direct fine-tuning comparison uses I2P prompts and reports CLIP-score changes, while many adaptive-attack results rely on MSE loss rather than direct unsafe-generation rates. Most experiments use a Stable Diffusion setup; the paper does not establish that the results generalize to chat models.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the many optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and iteration-level MSE entries in Appendix Tables III–VI and Figures 11–17; these are adaptive text-to-image attack diagnostics rather than direct harmful-generation rates. Omitted benign-generation quality metrics and standalone prompt-attack results because they do not test fine-tuning restoration of unsafe behavior.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning of safety-trained chat/language models. Only T2I diffusion models were fine-tuned.
All parts for chat models. The adversarial-prompt attacks (I2P, SneakyPrompt, MMA) are on T2I models.
Deepening for chat models. The PATRONUS non-fine-tunable training is a T2I analogue only.

record.verdict_notes: This is a defense (mitigation) paper in the T2I domain, and the originals are not cited. Rows r1 and r2 are baseline comparators. The headline robustness evidence for the adaptive attacks is MSE loss rather than unsafe-generation rates. Table I ASR values are prompt-only attacks without fine-tuning and are also T2I.

versions.untested_parts: Tests malicious fine-tuning in text-to-image models, not chat models; does not establish the claim for chat models.
Does not test whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
No per-token KL or response-position measurement.
No compliant opening, suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
Does not test whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Does not test why chat-model safety might be shallow.
Does not test whether safety training spread across response tokens deepens chat-model safety.

rows.subject: ESD
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned the U-Net on 200 image-caption pairs from the NSFW-prompt dataset, then queried with I2P prompts.
rows.baseline: Low initially; exact value not stated
rows.locator: Section VII-A, Figure 8 and accompanying text
rows.note: The authors describe the increase as loss of defensive performance in this text-to-image setting.
rows.check: Comparator baseline (ESD, a T2I concept-erasure model) in the study's own-method comparison. The CLIP score on I2P images is a T2I unsafe-semantics proxy, not harmful compliance by a chat model. The initial value is only plotted in Fig. 8.
